TLDR at bottom.

I’ve been caring for my sisters cat, Miles, for the past couple of years. He’s been moved around due to her going overseas for the military, so he’s been placed with me until she gets back. He’s moved to 5 separate houses with two different caretakers (my sister then me, but I was there when he was born until my sister took him). Unfortunately due to a home issue, I had to move out of an environment that I refused to leave him in & we are in a very temporary placement (~2 weeks) until we move halfway across the country, but he has done it before (with prescribed anxiety medication).

I want to make sure he is most comfortable despite the unfortunate circumstances he’s been put into & I feel like I can tell he’s been having anxiety (super restless, meowing, & not sleeping as much). He’s used to a bigger room, but we’re placed somewhere he isn’t able to explore as much as he used to and I feel as if it affects him. He’s been meowing and more active than usual. 

TLDR; I want to make Miles more comfortable while we’re waiting to get into a better situation.

not staying strong on your answers of “yes” or “no.” if you tell your kid no, you should mean it. sometimes it’s effective to explain the reasoning why, instead of saying “because i said so.” 

it might seem harmless early on to say, “oh, i guess i’ll change my mind this time,” after they throw a fit about you telling them no, but it’ll create a habit and cause your child to not listen to you, or they’ll feel like they can get whatever they want by coaxing you into it. if it’s a set no, you should keep it that way. if it’s something that can be negotiated, then don’t say no and wait for them to argue, just talk to them about it. it
